title: Thirteenth Toll
passages:
At the moment the pen left the twelfth mark, the ledger’s cord around Kornél’s wrist snapped tight once more. He seized Ákos’s trembling pen, pressed the nib, and felt the ink drink the stroke. A thin black tally appeared — the thirteenth mark — while his breath caught and his thoughts went blank. The name he had carried for years, the outline of Ilka on the landing, thinned to a smear. The ledger’s spine clicked, then released, and tightened anew as if waiting for payment.  

In the margin the word *River* quivered. Its letters rearranged, spreading a faint ripple outward like water over stone. Sára rose, her living hand slow as tide, forming the keeper’s sign for *enough* and pointing to the shifting word and to Ákos’s ghostly face. Márk nodded, flexing his own cold fingers, and gave the signal to carry the marks forward. Ruzsa swayed, eyes hollow, and whispered, “Fifteen more to the name.” Kornél’s voice grew rougher, warning, “The ledger keeps its word.”  

Ákos stepped to the page, pen already in hand, declaring he would write the next mark. The group turned their backs toward the under‑Point stone shelf, heading toward White Water, trusting the pilot’s channel and Sára’s cost.
